What We Do

One big service. Two that support it.

Revenue Cycle Management is the main service — the full journey from first form to paid claim. Secure forms and compliant communication are smaller services that support it.

The Main Service

Revenue Cycle Management

RCM is not a list of billing tasks. It is the full journey of a claim — and at every stage, that claim is in active exchange with the insurance company. Ovira manages both sides of that relationship, from the first eligibility inquiry to final adjudication and reconciliation, with AI claims management working inside the journey.

See how claims automation works inside RCM →

One claim, followed all the way through

A claim does not move in a straight line from your practice to a payment. It is created, questioned, priced, and decided through a continuing exchange with the payer — eligibility responses, authorization decisions, adjudication outcomes, remittance advice. Ovira stays inside that exchange at every stage, so the claim never sits unattended on either side.

Patient Access→ Authorization→ Coding→ Submission→ Adjudication→ Remittance→ Resolution
On the claimWhat Ovira does to move the claim forward accurately and on time.
With the payerHow the claim interacts with the insurance company at that same stage — what is sent, what comes back, and what Ovira does with the response.
  1. 01
    Before the visit · Patient Access

    Coverage is established

    Registration and insurance details captured at intake are verified before the encounter: active coverage, benefit structure, deductible and out-of-pocket status, and coordination of benefits where more than one plan applies. The claim's journey starts here — errors at this stage become denials weeks later.

    In practice: eligibility & benefits verification · financial clearance · COB determination

    With the payer

    Ovira submits an electronic eligibility inquiry and works from the payer's own response — plan status, coverage limits, and patient responsibility — not from the card alone. Where coverage is inactive, secondary, or restricted, that is resolved with the payer before care is billed, not after it is denied.

    Eligibility inquiry — 270Benefits response — 271
  2. 02
    Before care is delivered · Authorization

    Care is authorized

    Where the plan requires precertification, Ovira prepares and files the authorization request with supporting clinical documentation and medical-necessity justification, then tracks it to determination before the service is rendered.

    In practice: prior authorization · referral management · medical necessity documentation

    With the payer

    The payer's utilization review is a clinical conversation, not a formality. Ovira follows the request through review, supplies additional documentation on request, and supports peer-to-peer review where an initial determination is unfavourable — so an approved service is not later denied for lack of authorization.

    Authorization requestPayer determinationPeer-to-peer, if required
  3. 03
    After the encounter · Charge Capture & Coding

    The encounter becomes a claim

    Clinical documentation is translated into a complete, defensible claim: charges captured in full, diagnoses and procedures coded to specificity, and modifiers applied where the record supports them. Coding integrity here determines how the claim will be read downstream.

    In practice: charge capture · CPT / HCPCS · ICD-10-CM · modifier assignment · documentation integrity

    With the payer

    A claim is adjudicated against that payer's medical policy, bundling logic, and coverage criteria — so it is built to those rules before it leaves. Ovira aligns coding and supporting documentation with the contracted payer's policy for that service, reducing avoidable edits and medical-necessity denials at adjudication.

    Payer medical policyBundling & edit logic
  4. 04
    Submission · Clean Claim

    The claim is submitted clean

    Every claim is scrubbed against demographic, coding, and payer-specific edits before transmission, then submitted electronically within timely-filing limits. A clean-claim standard protects both payment speed and the practice's filing rights.

    In practice: claim scrubbing · claim edits · electronic submission — 837P / 837I · timely filing

    With the payer

    Submission is confirmed, not assumed. Clearinghouse and payer acknowledgements are reconciled daily; a rejected claim is corrected and resubmitted immediately rather than discovered weeks later as a silent no-response — the distinction between a rejection, handled in days, and a denial, handled in weeks.

    Claim — 837Acceptance — 277CARejections corrected & resubmitted
  5. 05
    In the payer's hands · Adjudication

    The payer adjudicates

    Once accepted, the claim enters adjudication — the payer prices it against the contracted fee schedule, applies benefit and deductible logic, and issues a determination. Ovira does not wait passively through this window; claim status is monitored throughout.

    In practice: adjudication · contracted allowable · claim status monitoring

    With the payer

    Through electronic claim-status inquiry, Ovira tracks each claim's position, identifies pended claims early, and responds promptly to payer requests for additional information or medical records — so a claim awaiting documentation is advanced, not aged in place.

    Status inquiry — 276Status response — 277Additional information, on request
  6. 06
    Determination issued · Remittance

    Remittance is reconciled

    The payer's remittance is posted line by line and reconciled to the claim as submitted: paid amounts, contractual adjustments, and patient-responsibility amounts are each verified. Payment alone is not the endpoint — payment accuracy is.

    In practice: payment posting · ERA / EOB reconciliation · contractual adjustment verification · underpayment identification

    With the payer

    Where the remitted amount differs from the contracted allowable, the variance is documented and raised with the payer rather than written off by default. Denial and adjustment reason codes on the remittance set the next action — correction, appeal, or transfer to patient responsibility.

    Remittance advice — ERA 835 / EOBReason codes — CO · PR · OA
  7. 07
    To final resolution · Denials & Patient Responsibility

    The claim is resolved

    A denied or partially paid claim is worked to root cause, then corrected, reconsidered, or formally appealed with supporting documentation — within the payer's appeal window. Any remaining patient responsibility is then billed accurately and compliantly, and accounts receivable is followed by age and payer until resolution.

    In practice: denial management · corrected claims · appeals & reconsiderations · A/R follow-up · patient statements

    With the payer

    Resolution is pursued through the payer's own process — reconsideration, documented appeal, and escalation where the determination conflicts with the contract or the record. Ovira carries the claim through that process to a final, defensible outcome: paid correctly, adjusted justifiably, or transferred properly — never simply left in the aging.

    Corrected claimFormal appealFinal determination
§

The journey ends at resolution — and informs the next claim

Every determination, denial reason, and contract variance feeds Ovira's reporting back to your practice: where revenue is performing, where payers are pushing back, and what changes upstream will prevent the same outcome on the next claim. That is the cycle in Revenue Cycle Management.

Watch It Work

One claim, station to station

No claim sits in a pile. Each automated station completes its step and hands the claim to the next — intake, client rules, submission, payer adjudication, and follow-up. Select any station to jump to it.

The handoff chain

The payer is shown as a generic node — the claim is worked the same careful way with every payer.

Claim
Intake receives the claim and validates the basics.

Every client, its own patient rules

There is no single standard rulebook. The rules are handled at ground level — the rules engine applies the patient rules of the client each claim belongs to.
